messages.content: When will be sunset in Beijing today?

function.name: calculate_sunrise
function.description: Calculate the time of sunrise for a specific date and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which sunrise time needs to be calculated.

date.description: The date for which sunrise time needs to be calculated in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not provided, current date is considered. Default: 1998-12-03

format.description: Format in which the time should be returned. If not provided, default format 'HH:MM' is considered.

message.content:
Sunset in Beijing today (July 20, 2026) is expected to occur at **about 19:10 local time** (Beijing Standard Time, UTC +8).  

> **Note:** This estimate is based on astronomical calculations for the date and location. Actual sunset times can vary slightly due to atmospheric refraction, topography, and the exact definition of “sunset” used by different services.
message.reasoning:
We need to compute sunset time for Beijing today. The user asks "When will be sunset in Beijing today?" We have a tool to calculate sunrise but not sunset. But we can approximate or use known data. However, the tool only calculates sunrise. There's no sunset function. We could compute sunset manually using sunrise and day length. But we don't have day length. Alternatively, we can approximate by adding daylight duration. But we don't know daylight duration.

We might respond that we cannot compute sunset with the given tool. Or we can approximate using typical day length for Beijing on this date. Today is July 20, 2026. In Beijing (latitude ~39.9 N), the sun rises around 5:30 and sets around 19:00. But we need more precise. Let's approximate: On July 20, the solar declination is about +23.44 * sin(360/365*(day_of_year - 81)). Day of year for July 20 is 201. So declination = 23.44*sin(360/365*(201-81)) = 23.44*sin(360/365*120) = 23.44*sin(93.97°). sin(93.97°)=0.998. So declination ≈ 23.44*0.998=23.41°. Latitude φ=39.90°. Hour angle at sunset H = arccos(-tanφ*tanδ). tanφ=tan(39.9°)=0.823; tanδ=tan(23.41°)=0.433. Product = -0.356. arccos(-0.356)=111.1°. Convert to hours: 111.1° /15 =7.407h. Solar noon at 12:00 local time? Actually Beijing Standard Time is UTC+8. Solar noon occurs when sun crosses meridian. At longitude 116.4°, solar noon offset from 12:00 is (longitude difference from Greenwich)/15 = 116.4/15=7.76h. So solar noon local time = 12:00 - 7.76h = 4.24h? Wait, that's wrong. Actually solar noon occurs when sun's hour angle zero. Local standard time noon is 12:00. The equation of time and longitude offset adjust. For Beijing, solar noon occurs earlier than 12:00 because it's east of GMT+8? Actually Beijing is at 116.4E, while GMT+8 corresponds to 120E. So Beijing is west of its standard meridian by 3.6°, so solar noon occurs later than 12:00 local time. So solar noon local time = 12:00 + (longitude difference)/15 = 12:00 + (-3.6/15) = 12:00 - 0.24h = 11:42. So solar noon ~11:42. Then sunrise = solar noon - H/15 = 11:42 - 7.407h = 4:14. Sunset = solar noon + H/15 = 11:42 + 7.407h = 19:09. So approximate sunset ~19:09 local time. That seems plausible. So answer: around 19:10 local time. Provide approximate. Also mention that due to equation of time, actual may differ slightly. Use approximate.
